ModelValidatorExternal.release_notes:
### PSSE Dynamics

- **New: Automatic Detection and Repair of Missing PLB Dynamics Models.** A PSSE test whose event requires a PLB-driven disturbance could previously run to completion and report success even though its selected DYR file had no active PLB model - silently producing a flat, event-less result. The app now checks for this at run time: if the selected DYR lacks an active PLB model, it automatically switches to a sibling DYR that has one, or - if none exists - generates one from an active GENCLS model in the case. Auto-generated files are clearly logged as not human-authored and should be reviewed before trusting compliance results that depend on them.

### Report Generation

- **Figure Captions and "Fig." Bookmarks Removed Under TocMode "None"/"Simple".** Every plot page previously printed a "Fig:X.Y TestID:..." caption and added a matching nested "Fig." bookmark, regardless of TocMode - redundant once each test already has its own unique TestID and a descriptive bookmark. These are now only generated under TocMode "Figures" or "Both", which actually build a List of Figures from them.
- **Report Header Line Breaks Are Now Preserved.** A multi-line Header (e.g. company name, project name, and study type typed on separate lines in the report config) was previously re-flowed into wrapped lines by width, discarding the line breaks you typed. Explicit line breaks are now preserved exactly as entered, in both PDF and Word reports.
- **Test Suite Name No Longer Printed on the First Plot Page Under TocMode "None".** Since the descriptive bookmarks already identify each test, the Test Suite Name heading is now omitted from the first page of each scenario when TocMode is "None".
- **Fixed: Plot Position Could Shift Between Pages Depending on Which Headings Were Shown.** The plot grid's position and size previously depended on whether the Title/Test Suite heading happened to be drawn on that particular page (e.g. suppressed under TocMode "None", or already shown earlier in a multi-page scenario). The space for these headings is now always reserved identically whether or not the text is actually drawn, so every plot sits at the same position and scale across all pages when scrolling through a report.

### Project Switching

- **Switch Project No Longer Restarts the Application.** Choosing "Switch Project" previously closed and relaunched the whole app. It now reopens the Project Manager dialog in place and switches directly to the newly selected project, without an application restart.
- **Project Switch Is Blocked While a Simulation or Report Is Running.** Attempting to switch projects while a simulation or report generation is in progress now shows a message asking you to wait, instead of switching out from under an active run.
- **Fixed: A Previous Project's Case File Could Be Reused After Switching.** When switching projects without a restart, a case path left over from the previously open project could, in rare cases, still exist on disk and get silently reused for the new project. Case restoration now confirms the stored case actually lives inside the newly opened project's own folder before reusing it, and clears the selection otherwise so it falls back to discovery.

### Multi-Engine Validation Benchmarking

- **Validation Auto-Mapping Now Supports Any Number of Simulation Engines at Once.** Previously, automatic channel mapping only ever paired one PSSE handler against one PSCAD handler. Projects running multiple PSSE variants together (e.g. PSSE_UDM and PSSE_GENERIC) now get each handler mapped independently, with every handler that resolves the same channel automatically grouped into one benchmark comparison - so PSSE_UDM vs PSSE_GENERIC, or PSCAD vs both PSSE variants at once, all validate correctly without manual reconfiguration.
- **Fixed: Benchmark Plots Could Show the Wrong Handler's Channel Settings.** When two handlers shared the same channel name (common when comparing two PSSE variants), the plotting engine could pull the scaling/config info for the wrong one. Channel lookups are now disambiguated by handler, so each curve always uses its own settings.

### Validation Test Fixes

- **Fixed: Several Validation Tests Ignored Their Configured Time Tolerance.** Active Power Recovery, Reactive Power Rise Time, Voltage Rise Time, Reactive Current Response, Active Power Response, and the MISO balanced-fault-ride-through and VRT tests were reading a kwarg key that didn't match the configured field name, so the time-tolerance value from validation configuration was silently ignored (always `None`) even when set. These tests now correctly apply the configured time tolerance.

It now shows a confirmation dialog explaining that customisations will be overwritten, before proceeding.
